title: U.S. House · North Carolina's 7th District
area: Southeastern North Carolina, including Wilmington and Fayetteville.

context.text: Incumbent David Rouzer (R) advanced from a contested Republican primary. Kimberly Hardy advanced from a canceled Democratic primary. Maad Abu-Ghazalah advanced from a canceled Libertarian primary. Independent Michael Henry did not make the general-election ballot.

candidates.name: David Rouzer

summary.text: David Rouzer is the Republican incumbent seeking re-election in North Carolina's 7th Congressional District. He chairs the Transportation and Infrastructure Committee's Highways and Transit Subcommittee and previously served in the North Carolina State Senate.

background.text: Born on a U.S. Army base in Landstuhl, Germany, in 1972; earned a bachelor's degree in agricultural business management, agricultural economics and chemistry from North Carolina State University in 1994.

Worked as an aide to Sens. Jesse Helms (R) and Elizabeth Dole (R), at North Carolina State University's College of Agriculture and Life Sciences, and as an associate administrator for the U.S. Department of Agriculture; owned The Rouzer Company.
Served in the North Carolina State Senate from 2009 to 2012.

positions.summary: In a September 2021 statement, opposed H.R. 3755, legislation to preempt almost all state and federal restrictions on abortion, and said he will keep fighting for pro-life protections.
positions.quote: I strongly oppose the extreme abortion bill brought to the House floor today that allows abortion for any reason, at any stage of pregnancy, even until right before birth.

positions.summary: In a June 2023 statement, supported overturning the ATF pistol-brace rule as an infringement on gun owners' rights.
positions.quote: The Biden Administration's unconstitutional pistol brace rule infringes on the Second Amendment rights of millions of law-abiding gun owners, including many disabled combat veterans

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Agriculture, the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure, where he chairs the Highways and Transit Subcommittee and is vice chair of the General Farm Commodities, Risk Management, and Credit Subcommittee, and the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology.

candidates.researchNotes: Federal key votes and FEC totals for this sitting member of Congress are added separately. No specific 2026 campaign priorities were located within the research budget beyond his committee assignments.

candidates.name: Kimberly Hardy
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from a canceled Democratic primary.

summary.text: Kimberly Hardy is the Democratic nominee challenging incumbent David Rouzer in North Carolina's 7th Congressional District. She is a social work professor who has previously run for this seat.

background.text: Earned a bachelor's degree from Morgan State University (1997), a master's in social work from Ohio State University, and a Ph.D. in social work from Morgan State University.
Has worked as an assistant professor of social work at Fayetteville State University, the University of Saint Joseph (2013-2016), and the University of Connecticut (2010-2013).

priorities.text: Putting education first, saying the North Carolina General Assembly has left schools and students stuck in the Great Recession.

positions.summary: In a Port City Daily questionnaire, said she would fund a tax cut for lower earners with a surtax on incomes over $1 million and an excise tax on large corporations that do not pay a living wage.
positions.quote: I would pay for this cut by putting a tiered surtax on incomes over $1 million per year.

positions.summary: In a Port City Daily questionnaire, said the administration needs congressional approval for continued military action in Iran.
positions.quote: Yes, absolutely, the administration needs Congressional approval for continued military action in Iran.

positions.summary: On her campaign site, lists raising the federal minimum wage among the things she supports.
positions.quote: Raising the federal minimum wage for the first time in nearly 30 years.

positions.summary: In her 2020 Ballotpedia survey (for a state House race, not this race), listed expanding Medicaid as a key campaign message. Dated: she has not completed a 2026 survey.
positions.quote: Expanding Medicaid - at zero additional cost to North Carolinians, we can help 500,000 people access health care

candidates.researchNotes: Positions combine her 2026 Port City Daily questionnaire, her campaign site's priorities page, and her 2020 Ballotpedia survey (state House race; no 2026 survey completed). Her answers did not address abortion, guns, immigration enforcement stance, school choice, or Israel aid directly.

statements.quote: Support homegrown energy initiatives including solar, wind, and geothermal.
statements.context: On her campaign website, under Environment

statements.quote: Congress could have ended the tariffs, kept the administration from dragging on the release of the Epstein files, and blocked expensive, rash actions like paying billions in kill fees to clean energy projects. It just takes courage.
statements.context: In the Port City Daily 2026 candidate questionnaire

statements.quote: We should be looking into the mistakes that led to ICE killing American citizens, to immigration agencies hiring members of MS-13.

candidates.name: Maad Abu-Ghazalah
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from a canceled Libertarian Party primary.

summary.text: Maad Abu-Ghazalah is the Libertarian Party nominee in North Carolina's 7th Congressional District. He is a consultant campaigning as an anti-war, fiscally conservative candidate.

background.text: Earned a bachelor's degree from the University of Notre Dame (1983), a graduate degree from the University of Virginia (1985), and a law degree from Santa Clara University (1993); works as a consultant.

priorities.text: Ending U.S. involvement in foreign wars he says have nothing to do with national interest.
Balancing the federal budget and opposing what he calls irresponsible money printing.
Protecting civil liberties, particularly free speech.

positions.summary: On his campaign site, says the U.S. should stop arming Israel and other foreign governments and use diplomacy instead.
positions.quote: We need to stop arming Israel and other foreign regimes like Egypt, Jordan and the Ukraine and start using our leverage to create peace in the world through diplomacy.

candidates.researchNotes: Positions drawn from his 2026 Ballotpedia survey and campaign website (getmaad.org). A Feb. 2026 press release carrying his quotes was issued by the Libertarian Party of North Carolina (not his campaign) and was not used. Other issues are not addressed in the material found.
